prompt:
Edit this photo. It shows a real street in Pereslavl-Zalessky, an ancient small town in central Russia; the street leads down to the shore of Lake Pleshcheyevo. Keep the camera exactly as it is: same viewpoint, height, lens, perspective and framing, same sunny sky. Make it late May: trees in fresh early-summer leaf. The red and blue outlines are reference marks only and must be completely removed from the result. Keep the tall spruces on the left and the low private houses in the background.

BLUE OUTLINE (left side): the long two-storey building is restored, not replaced. Keep its volume, roofline, the three small gables on the roof and the rhythm of its large windows. Walls are repainted in a warm limestone white with a slightly darker plinth; the roof is dark grey standing-seam metal. Windows become multi-pane frames in thin dark green painted timber, in the same rhythm as now. The red cladding band and the white plastic shop entrance are removed: the supermarket stays, but behind windows that match the rest of the facade, with only small, discreet lettering. Next to it, a bakery and a bicycle rental open onto the street.

RED OUTLINE (right side): the two-storey apartment house is restored, not replaced. The patchwork of plaster and bare brick becomes one even lime render in a muted warm ochre, with white window surrounds and a white cornice. The slate roof is replaced with dark grey standing-seam metal. Windows are new timber frames, air-conditioning units are hidden.

STREET: the whole street is rebuilt as a single-level, low-speed street where pedestrians and cyclists have priority and cars are guests. There are no curbs and no level changes anywhere: the carriageway, the walking areas and the building edges all lie on one continuous surface. The narrow carriageway is smooth dark asphalt, set apart from the walking areas only by a flush strip of grey granite and by the line of trees and planting, with small bicycle symbols painted on it. The walking areas on both sides are paved with large light-grey concrete slabs.

All overhead wires and utility poles are gone; utilities run underground. The concrete slabs lying by the roadside are removed. No bare soil or dusty ground is left anywhere in the frame.

Water: on both sides, long planted rain gardens run between the carriageway and the walking areas, set clearly lower than all surrounding paving. Rainwater from the whole street reaches them through shallow open channels of grey granite set flush into the paving, so you can see where the water goes. The rain gardens are planted as a dense native meadow of central Russia — meadow grasses, sedges, wild geranium, yarrow, meadowsweet — with clumps of red-stemmed dogwood, wild rose and shrubby willow, not as a mown lawn.

Trees: the existing trees on the right are kept and have grown full natural crowns. A continuous row of young linden trees runs along both sides, planted flush within the paving, so the street will become a shaded avenue toward the lake.

In front of the long building there are only two or three parking spaces and a loading bay, paved with permeable concrete blocks with gravel joints. Along the walking areas: a few simple timber benches on dark steel frames, plain steel bicycle racks, a drinking fountain and a slim wayfinding post with an arrow pointing toward the lake. Low pedestrian lamp posts in dark grey with warm, downward-facing light. The green corrugated metal fence in the background is replaced with a simple dark-stained timber board fence.

People: a few residents walk toward the lake, a cyclist rides down the middle of the carriageway, a child on a scooter, someone sitting on a bench outside the bakery.

Overall mood: quiet, clean, precise and generous to people on foot — a contemporary, well-engineered street in an old Russian town, not a stage set. Palette of limestone white, muted ochre, dark green, light grey, granite and natural timber. Avoid bright colours, red cycle lanes, plastic cladding, glazed balconies, folk-style kitsch, onion domes, carved fretwork added where there was none, and European postcard clichés such as cobblestones, faux-vintage lanterns, flower pots and decorative bollards with chains.
notes: Версия без реагентов: улица в одном уровне, без бордюров, вода уходит в дождевые сады.

prompt:
Edit this photo. It shows the centre of Tsimlyansk, a small town on the Lower Don in the Rostov region of southern Russia, known for its wines and the Tsimlyansk Reservoir. Keep the camera exactly as it is: same viewpoint, height, lens, perspective and framing, including the foreground; same bright summer light. Keep the tall poplars on the right and the low houses in the far background.

The coloured marks are instructions only and must be completely removed from the result:
- RED outline: demolish and replace (described below).
- BLUE outline: reconstruct (described below).
- GREEN outline: restore (described below).
- YELLOW marks: utility poles, overhead wires and a billboard. Remove them entirely. In the finished image the sky is completely clear: there are no utility poles, no wires and no billboard anywhere.

RED OUTLINE (left foreground): the kiosks are demolished. In their place stands an open market pavilion: a long, low-pitched roof of dark metal on slender timber posts, with no walls, giving deep shade. Underneath are simple timber stalls selling fruit, vegetables, fish from the reservoir and local wine, with a few shoppers and stallholders.

BLUE OUTLINE (left, behind the pavilion): the supermarket is reconstructed, not replaced. Keep its footprint and height. The grey composite panels are gone: the walls are pale sandstone and sand-coloured brick under a low-pitched hipped roof of dark metal with a generous overhang. Along the whole ground floor runs a deep arcade of plain square brick piers, clearly visible behind and beside the market roof, with shopfronts in its shade. Large upper windows in a calm, regular rhythm. Only small, discreet lettering; the red signage and all posters are removed.

GREEN OUTLINE (right): the yellow single-storey building is restored, not replaced. Keep its volume, pilasters and window rhythm. Walls in a softer, muted ochre yellow; pilasters, window surrounds and cornice in white; roof in dark grey standing-seam metal. New timber windows. No air-conditioning units are visible on the facade. Posters and poster stands are removed.

STREET LEVEL: the whole street and square form one continuous, perfectly level surface. A narrow carriageway of smooth dark asphalt lies at exactly the same height as the paving around it, joined by a flat strip of grey granite that a stroller rolls across without any bump. There are no curbs, no kerbstones and no raised edges anywhere in the image. The surplus asphalt becomes a small town square in front of the market and the supermarket, paved with large pale sandstone-coloured concrete slabs. The pedestrian crossing is simply a band of contrasting paving across the level surface. Only the necessary road signs remain.

RAIN GARDENS: long rain gardens run along both sides of the carriageway. They are shallow sunken hollows: their edges are flush with the paving, with no borders, frames or raised rims, and the planting sits visibly below the level of the walkway. Rainwater reaches them through shallow open granite channels set flush into the paving. They are densely planted with drought-tolerant plants of the Don steppe — feather grass, sage, yarrow, lavender, low tamarisk shrubs — over grey gravel mulch. No bare soil or dusty ground anywhere in the frame.

SHADE: over the walkways on both sides, light steel pergolas form a continuous roof of grapevines overhead, so people walk and sit in green shade beneath them. The poplars are kept, with no white paint on their trunks. Young plane trees and mulberry trees are planted flush within the paving around the square.

DETAILS: only a few cars remain, in a short row of parking spaces with permeable paving. Simple timber benches in the shade, plain steel bicycle racks, a drinking fountain, low dark grey lamp posts with warm downward light. People shop at the market, sit in the shade under the vines, cross the street at an easy pace; someone rides a bicycle.

Overall mood: unhurried, sunlit but shaded, clean and precise — the centre of a southern Russian wine town that looks after itself, not a stage set. Palette of pale sandstone, sand brick, muted ochre, white, dark metal and the green of vines and trees. Avoid bright colours, plastic or composite cladding, Cossack or folk-style kitsch, decorative wine barrels or cartwheels, and European postcard clichés such as cobblestones, faux-vintage lanterns, flower pots and café parasols.
notes: Вторая попытка, с жёлтой разметкой проводов, столбов и щита. В первой модель оставила провода, рекламный щит и приподнятые бортики у клумб.
